title: Regional SLI Ownership Heatmap + Chaos Injector for Token-Level Load Shedding
creator: Priya Ramakrishnan
description: Build a combined observability-and-injection initiative that: (1) surfaces per-region, per-shard ownership for token-level SLIs via a heatmap so oncall and SREs can quickly see where latency or admit changes originate; and (2) provides a lightweight chaos injector that can ramp synthetic load and simulate regional degradation and admission cutoffs to validate circuit-breaker and load-shedding behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Heatmap dashboard shows p50/p95/p99 token latency, admit rate, KV hit rate, and active circuit state per-region and per-shard with filtering by model and route.
2) Chaos injector can simulate 3 modes: (a) microburst of short high-qps requests, (b) KV cache cold-start on a shard, (c) controlled region-level network partition (simulated by increasing latency/failure).
3) Runbook updated with playbook steps for triage using the heatmap.
4) Two canary runs executed against staging with automated regression checks: no unhandled cascades and circuit fallback triggers within expected thresholds.
5) Metrics retention and cost impact assessment documented.
decisions:
- Use sampled token-level telemetry for heatmap (1% sampling) to limit cardinality and cost.
- Compute admit rate and latency in an offline rollup job to avoid high-cardinality live queries; rollups updated every 30s.
- Chaos injector implemented as a Kubernetes Job + small harness service that issues real requests through ingress to preserve routing behavior, not a synthetic bypass.
- Circuit state will be annotated on the heatmap via correlated throttling events emitted by the admission service.
- Initial rollout restricted to two non-prod regions and one production region to limit blast radius.
tasks:
1) Instrument token-level sampled events to include shard_id, region, model, route, kv_hit boolean, admit_decision, token_latency_ms. (owner: Carlos)
2) Build rollup service to aggregate sampled events into 30s buckets and write to metrics store (owner: Mei-Lin)
3) Heatmap dashboard: Grafana panels with heat tile + drilldown to traces (owner: Sasha)
4) Chaos injector: implement modes + safety guardrails and abort on SLO regression (owner: Anton)
5) Runbook and playbook updates + oncall training session (owner: Priya)
6) Canary plan + automated checks GitHub Actions workflow (owner: DevOps)
7) Post-mortem template and experiment logging (owner: Carlos)

comments: 2025-11-05 — Priya: Kickoff complete. Alignment with SRE: use sampling to control cardinality; SRE asked for ability to immediately pivot to full sampling for short windows during incidents.

2025-11-06 — Carlos: Added initial proto schema for sampled token events in repo. Note: including raw token text is forbidden; only token_id and token_length retained. Open question: include user/customer_id hashed? (security asked to minimize PII).

2025-11-07 — Mei-Lin: Rollup job prototype writes to TSDB using series: region.shard.model.route.metric. We will add a coarse-grain tag for 'priority_class' to aid SLO mapping. Perf test shows ~18% added ingestion cost at 1% sampling.

2025-11-09 — Sasha: Dashboard draft ready. Using heatmap plugin to show shard x region matrix. Added drilldown to trace explorer linking to X-Request-ID. Need backend support to ensure sampled events attach request id header.
2025-11-10 — Anton: Chaos harness initial mode implemented (microburst). Safety: abort when p99 token latency > 2x baseline for 2 consecutive windows. Will add opt-in gating for prod runs.
2025-11-11 — Security (Aisha): Confirmed sampled events schema acceptable if customer_id is hashed using HMAC with per-tenant salt. Put note in decision log.

2025-11-12 — Priya: Ran staging canary with microburst mode. Heatmap surfaced shard-3 in eu-west with KV hit drop; circuit breaker correctly flipped to degraded variant and traffic routed to fallback region. Follow-up: improve labeling for fallback reasoning in dashboard tooltip.
